purpose: Independent literal synthetic development contracts for bounded whole-group P2/P3; not fresh final holdout or field evidence.
authorship: Written before P2 engine edits using the approved scope and existing public API/test shape only. Expected memberships and signed totals are authored from literal source facts, not engine results.

cases.title: A whole bank-identified payment in 1:N form
cases.rationale: One explicit bank identity names the complete -900 payment and both -250/-650 parts. Require the full group, without inventing row-level allocation.

cases.title: The same complete payment in N:1 form
cases.rationale: Reversing export sides preserves the same economic payment group.

cases.title: Whole bank-identified N:M payment equivalence
cases.rationale: Every row is Payment with the same explicit bank identity. Both complete sides total -900; the required relation is the two whole member sets, not arbitrary pairs.

cases.title: Whole receipt-identified N:M without bank evidence
cases.rationale: An explicitly labelled Receipt No names the entire payment on each side; bank values are absent.

cases.title: Two identity roles corroborate exactly the same members
cases.rationale: The bank and receipt buckets have identical full memberships. They support one group rather than two competing consumptions.

cases.title: The 1000/500 example resolves identities and rejects the equal-sum decoy
cases.rationale: INV-A is 1000 against its 400+600 lines with a shared PO. INV-B is the separate 500 pair. INV-C is a different reference, so B+C cannot become an A group even though their sum is 1000.

cases.title: Invoice subgroup works in reverse  N:1 direction
cases.rationale: The same complete invoice subgroups and unmatched INV-C remain when export roles reverse; each valid invoice group retains its shared PO.

cases.title: Permutation preserves complete bank-group membership
cases.rationale: Source row positions differ from P2D03, but all original bank identity members remain. Whole economic membership and totals must be unchanged.

cases.title: Overlapping bank and receipt memberships remain unresolved
cases.rationale: BANK-460 spans the first two rows; RCPT-X spans the first and third. The identity-role memberships overlap and disagree, even though each side has the same amounts. No role may greedily consume a subset.

cases.title: A manual pair does not remove an original overlapping competitor
cases.rationale: The accountant explicitly pairs source row 2 on each side. The remaining original bank/receipt overlap still exists for automatic eligibility; consumed rows cannot create artificial uniqueness.

manualPairs.note: Explicit synthetic accountant confirmation for this pair only

cases.title: A duplicated component is not proof of two distinct payment parts
cases.rationale: Two -50 lines in the ledger are identical, including their local voucher. They cannot be assumed distinct parts merely because their sum is -100.

cases.title: An unknown document type blocks whole payment approval
cases.rationale: One purported part has a type not established as Payment. Its amount and bank identity cannot prove its accounting role.

cases.title: An excluded same-identity member remains relevant to completeness
cases.rationale: An extra -20 ledger row shares the bank identity but lies after cutoff. Dropping it makes the remaining amounts appear equal; this cannot approve the incomplete original group.

cases.title: A different row currency cannot contribute to a SAR group
cases.rationale: The -60 part is explicitly USD while scope and remaining rows are SAR. It must be a visible row error, with no automatic payment group.

cases.title: Offsetting signs cannot manufacture a payment split
cases.rationale: -150 and +50 net to -100 but do not form same-direction parts of the same payment. The balancing sum does not establish membership.

cases.title: A same-identity part outside the date window remains unresolved
cases.rationale: One part is five days after the payment date while the declared window is three days. Both are inside cutoff; do not confuse cutoff validity with grouping date evidence.

cases.title: Amounts and generic references alone cannot create payment groups
cases.rationale: No explicitly labelled bank or receipt identity exists. Several parts and equal-sum alternatives are visible, but no automatic group is justified.

cases.title: A complete group above the declared 100-member side limit is not approved
cases.rationale: The ledger has 101 distinct posting vouchers of -1 each. The identity and sum are otherwise valid, but this case deliberately exceeds the declared whole-group side limit. A visible limit explanation is required.

cases.title: The exact 100-member boundary remains a supported positive
cases.rationale: Exactly 100 ledger parts, each carrying its own distinct voucher, share one bank identity and total -100. The declared boundary is inclusive.
